label: Pride and teasing
rationale: Looking foolish or cool: being made fun of, embarrassing yourself, and showing off.
mixUps: Making fun of someone is baka ni suru (baka ni shinaide), not warau. haji o kaku uses the same kaku as ase o kaku. kakko tsukeru is acting cool, while kakko ii is being cool.

targets.english: make fun of, look down on
targets.verbSense: do; with X ni, treat as or make into X
targets.trap: English 'make fun of' leads to karakau, which is right for playful teasing but too light for contempt. Mocking someone or treating them as stupid is baka ni suru.
partners: nakamahazure (leaving someone out: nakamahazure ni sareta)
targets.use: Heard most in protest: baka ni shinaide (don't make fun of me), baka ni shiteru no? (are you mocking me?), and in the passive, baka ni sareta (they made fun of me). It covers both mocking and treating someone as stupid.
targets.notes: baka ni dekinai = not to be underestimated: konbini no bentou, baka ni dekinai yo.

examplePolite.ja: バカにしないでください。
examplePolite.english: Please don't make fun of me.

targets.english: embarrass yourself, make a fool of yourself
targets.verbSense: scratch; with sweat, snoring or shame, give off or come out in
targets.trap: English 'I embarrassed myself' leads to jibun o hazukashiku shita, which isn't said. The incident is haji o kaku (the kaku of ase o kaku, not kaku 'write'); hazukashikatta is how it felt.
targets.use: Mostly told after the fact: minna no mae de haji o kaita (I made a fool of myself in front of everyone), with o kept far more often than in most sets, though haji kaita is heard too. Making someone else look bad is haji o kakaseru: haji o kakasenaide yo (don't embarrass me).
targets.notes: hazukashii is the feeling; haji o kaku is the incident that causes it.

example.romaji: minna no mae de haji o kaita.
example.ja: みんなの前で恥をかいた。
example.english: I made a fool of myself in front of everyone.

examplePolite.romaji: minna no mae de haji o kakimashita.
examplePolite.ja: みんなの前で恥をかきました。
examplePolite.english: I embarrassed myself in front of everyone.

targets.verbSense: attach, put on; here, put on a look or front
targets.trap: English 'show off' leads to jiman suru, which is bragging in words about what you have or did. Putting on a cool act is kakko tsukeru, and the long-vowel kakkou o suru is about clothes: hen na kakkou shiteru (you're dressed weird).
targets.use: Said with the short vowel and no o: kakko tsukenaide (quit posing), kakko tsuketeru dake (he's just trying to look cool). A poser is a kakkotsuke. The dictionary form is kakkou o tsukeru (格好をつける).
targets.notes: kakkoii (cool) and kakkowarui (uncool, embarrassing) are built on the same noun.

example.ja: かっこつけなくていいよ。
example.english: You don't need to act cool.

examplePolite.ja: かっこつけなくていいですよ。
examplePolite.english: There's no need to put on a show.

reviewPool.english: have no motivation, can't be bothered
